Register
rĕj'ĭs-tēr
n. (a written roll or record; in Ezra and Nehemiah, the genealogical roll of the returning exiles)
Late Latin registrum, from regerere, to record or enter. In Scripture it is always a document of descent, and it decides who may serve.

Biblical Definition

Nehemiah, moved of God to number the people, says: “I found a register of the genealogy of them which came up at the first, and found written therein” (Neh 7:5) — and the list follows, family by family, with the number of each. The document mattered because of a specific problem recorded twice in identical words: certain priestly families “sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood” (Ezr 2:62; Neh 7:64). Men who believed themselves priests, who had come all the way from Babylon to serve, were barred because the roll did not have them. The Tirshatha ruled that they should not eat of the most holy things till there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim. Under the old covenant, descent was everything for the priesthood; a man could not volunteer into Aaron's line. That is precisely the problem the epistle to the Hebrews raises about Christ, who sprang out of Judah, of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood — and answers with a priest after the order of Melchisedec, made not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life. The register was real, and it pointed past itself.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a register as a written account or entry of acts, judgments or proceedings; a book of public records; also the officer who keeps the record.

expand to see more

REGISTER, n. A written account or entry of acts, judgments or proceedings, for preserving and conveying to future times an exact knowledge of transactions.

2. The book of records; a book in which entries are made.

3. The officer or person whose business is to write and keep the register.

Key Scripture

Neh 7:5 — "And my God put into mine heart to gather together the nobles, and the rulers, and the people, that they might be reckoned by genealogy. And I found a register of the genealogy of them which came up at the first, and found written therein,"

Ezr 2:62 — "These sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."

Rev 20:15 — "And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire."

Modern Corruption

Religious identity is now built on self-description — a man is what he sincerely considers himself to be — and the register stands in Scripture as the refusal of that principle at its most painful.

expand to see more

Ezra 2:62 is a hard verse and it is meant to be. Men had made the journey from Babylon believing themselves to be priests. They may well have been sincere; nothing in the text calls them liars. But when the roll was searched their names were not in it, and they were put from the priesthood as polluted. Sincerity was not the standard; enrolment was. That principle offends a culture in which identity is understood to be constituted by inward conviction and public declaration, so that to question a man's account of himself is treated as an offence against him. Scripture does not work that way about anything that matters. The Lord Jesus said that many would say to Him in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? — men entirely persuaded of their standing — and His answer is, I never knew you. The book of life in Revelation 20:15 is the register of which Ezra's roll was the shadow, and the same rule governs: not found written. This is not a counsel of despair, because unlike a Babylonian genealogy the book of life is not entered by descent at all, and the way in is published openly — whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely. But it is entered God's way, and a man's certainty about himself is not the register.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew kethab (H3791), a writing, a register; yachas (H3187), to reckon by genealogy, to enrol; Greek biblos tes zoes, the book of life.

expand to see more

Hebrew kethab (H3791) — a writing, an edict, a register; the roll Nehemiah found; Nehemiah 7:5, Esther 3:14.

Hebrew yachas (H3187) — to reckon by genealogy, to enrol; the verb that decided a priest's standing; Ezra 2:62, 1 Chronicles 5:17.

Greek biblos (G976) — a book, a scroll; the book of life in which names are written from the foundation of the world; Revelation 20:15, Philippians 4:3.

Usage

"“I found a register of the genealogy of them which came up at the first” — Nehemiah's roll of the returning exiles."

"“They were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood” — sincerity was not the standard."

"“Whosoever was not found written in the book of life” — the register of which Ezra's roll was the shadow."
